name: Guo Yiqun
current_role: Shareholder of Shanghai PRET Composites (SZSE: 002324); spouse of founder/chairman Zhou Wen
profile: Guo Yiqun is the wife of Zhou Wen, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Shanghai PRET Composites, a Shanghai maker of modified plastics and composites (largely automotive-grade PP, ABS, PA, LCP). Her Hurun wealth is shared with Zhou Wen and derives from the family's PRET stake. She keeps no public profile of her own.
interesting_fact: PRET's 2009 IPO prospectus lists Guo Yiqun as one of the company's founding promoter shareholders; with Zhou Wen and two relatives she held 77.84% of PRET before its 2009 Shenzhen listing.
deep_cut_fact: She became a PRET shareholder in a November 2002 capital increase, when the company's registered capital went from RMB2m to RMB20m; she contributed RMB1.306m in cash for a 6.53% stake.
notes: Very private, with no media presence; the best route is through PRET's board office (dsh@ is the board secretary's mailbox listed in the 2009 prospectus, so confirm it is still current). Zhou Wen is the public face. Hurun listing through 2026 suggests she is living, but no direct confirmation was found.

name: Roger Federer
current_role: Retired tennis champion (20 Grand Slam singles titles); investor in On Holding; co-founder of Laver Cup/TEAM8; founder of the Federer Foundation
profile: Swiss tennis great who won 20 Grand Slam singles titles and more than $130m in prize money before retiring in 2022. His fortune came mostly from endorsements (Uniqlo's 10-year, $300m deal; Rolex; Mercedes) and an estimated ~3% stake in Swiss shoemaker On, which listed in 2021. He now focuses on investing, the Laver Cup with agent Tony Godsick's TEAM8, and his foundation.
interesting_fact: Federer was the world's highest-paid athlete in 2020, earning an estimated $106.3m pre-tax. Most of it came from endorsements, which at his peak brought in $100m a year off the court.
deep_cut_fact: Before winning a record 10 Swiss Indoors titles, Federer worked as a ball boy at the same Basel tournament in 1992-93. As champion he later threw a pizza party for the event's ball kids.

public_contacts.value: TEAM8 (his management company, co-founded with Tony Godsick): info@team8global.com
contact@federerfoundation.org (Federer Foundation; only for enquiries related to the foundation's work)

notes: Heavily managed. Media and business requests go through TEAM8 (Tony Godsick). The foundation states it accepts no unsolicited proposals or autograph requests. For an entrepreneurship angle, the On investment and TEAM8/Laver Cup are the natural hooks.

name: Tang Zhengqing
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder (about 20% direct) of Jiahe Foods Industry (SSE: 605300; brand Cograin)
profile: Tang Zhengqing and her husband Liu Xinrong, Jiahe Foods' controlling shareholder and chairman, are the company's actual controllers. Jiahe, founded in 2001 in Wujiang, Suzhou, is a leading Chinese maker of non-dairy creamer for milk tea, coffee and baking, plus coffee and other solid beverages. It listed in Shanghai in 2021. She holds no executive role and keeps a low profile.
interesting_fact: Jiahe's 2025 interim report lists her as the company's second-largest shareholder, with 92.16m shares (20.28%) held directly, next to her husband's 28.39%.
notes: Very private. No interviews or biography found, and the public face of the company is Liu Xinrong. The best route is Jiahe's IR or board-secretary office. Hurun last listed her in 2023. Alive status was not independently confirmed, though she is named as a shareholder in 2025 filings.

name: Zhou Guoying
current_role: Co-actual controller and adviser, Ningbo Zhongda Leader Intelligent Transmission (SZSE: 002896); legal representative of controlling holder Ningbo Zhongda Lide Investment
profile: Zhou Guoying (b. 1970) co-controls Zhongda Leader with her husband Cen Guojian, its chairman and GM. The Cixi, Ningbo company makes precision reducers, small and special motors and drive units used in industrial robots, logistics automation and new-energy equipment. She was a director from 2006 until her term ended in August 2025, and she now serves as company adviser.
interesting_fact: The company she co-controls makes precision reducers, servo/small motors and drive units for industrial robots, intelligent logistics and new-energy equipment. She and her husband first appeared on Hurun's China Rich List in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zhongda existed, she was finance department manager at Zhanyun Machinery (1998 to July 2006), the predecessor workshop her husband ran as managing partner. She then served as a director of Zhongda from 2006.
notes: Low profile. The 2025 annual report lists her as company adviser and co-actual controller, so she is presumed alive. Board secretary Wu Xujun handles IR. Robotics and automation is a good podcast angle. Cen Guojian is the public face.

name: Chung Te-Li
current_role: Chairman, Lai Yih Footwear Group (TWSE: 6890, Lai Yih-KY)
profile: Chung Te-Li (also written 鐘德禮) co-founded Taichung-based Lai Yih in 1987. It makes vulcanized casual shoes and cold-cemented athletic shoes for adidas (about 58% of sales), Converse and HOKA, in factories in Vietnam, China, Myanmar and Indonesia with more than 55,000 staff. The company listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in June 2025, and he still chairs it.
interesting_fact: Lai Yih is the low-profile factory behind hit sneakers such as the adidas Samba and the HOKA shoes Joe Biden was photographed wearing. Rather than follow rivals into China, it went to Vietnam early, opening in Ho Chi Minh City in 1990.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating he worked 11 years in Taiwanese shoe factories, where he was struck by the quality and production-management standards adidas brought through its agents. In 1987 he co-founded Lai Yih with five friends, including president Lin Chang-yung, who was still his partner more than 37 years later.
notes: The surname appears as both 鍾 and 鐘 in media. Company spokesperson is Hsu Sung-chu. He gives occasional comments at shareholder meetings, for example on the roughly US$100m Indonesian plant. The IR email comes from a market-data site, so check it against MOPS before sending.

name: Chen Jiangyue
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Xu Buyun) of Buyang Group and Buyang International Holding (HKEX: 2457)
profile: Chen Jiangyue is the wife and business partner of Xu Buyun, who founded Yongkang, Zhejiang-based Buyang Group. The group started as a small foundry and grew into security doors (Buyang doors), vehicles, real estate, auto parts and logistics. The couple's aluminium-wheel arm, Buyang International, listed in Hong Kong in December 2022. She holds no board seat and keeps no public profile.
interesting_fact: Buyang's 'BYW' aluminium alloy wheel business sold more than one million wheels in 2020 to customers in over 50 countries. It began in 2005 by targeting the overseas aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The HK prospectus says she co-founded the wheel subsidiary Buyang Wheel with her husband in 2007. Before the IPO reorganisation she owned 30% of the wheel holding company to his 70%.
notes: Very private. Xu Buyun, chairman and non-executive director of Buyang International, is the public face, so the best route is through the company secretary or IR of HKEX: 2457. Her last Hurun appearance was 2021. No death reports found, but she was not confirmed alive.

name: Yuan Kaifei
profile: Hurun lists Yuan Kaifei (袁凯飞) under 'Newcentury Shipbuilding'. New Century Shipyard was a private yard in Jingjiang, Jiangsu, that formed a JV with a Singapore company in 2004; New Times Shipbuilding absorbed its assets in 2006. No source found confirming Yuan Kaifei's role at either company.
notes: Could not verify this person's role in English or Chinese searches; Baidu Baike is blocked. He was on Hurun China 2008-2021, with his last appearance in 2021. Check the Chinese company registry (qcc/tianyancha) for New Times / New Century Shipbuilding shareholders before any outreach. Background on the yard: https://www.lr.org/en/shipyards/china/new-times-shipbuilding-co-ltd/

name: Guo Peng
profile: Hurun lists Guo Peng (郭鹏) as the owner behind Puyang Iron and Steel, the private Hebei Puyang Iron & Steel (part of Hebei Puyang Industrial Group) in Yangyi Town, Wu'an, Handan. In 2020 it was named one of the five groups into which Wu'an planned to consolidate its 14 steelmakers. No public source found confirming his title.
interesting_fact: In Wu'an's 2020 consolidation plan, which merged 14 local steel companies into five groups, Puyang Iron and Steel was chosen as one of the five surviving group platforms.
notes: Could not confirm his role. Baidu and the company site (pygt.cn) were unreachable. His last Hurun appearance was 2021. The company is private and unlisted, so it has no IR channel. Verify through a Chinese corporate registry before outreach. Low-priority, very private.

name: Zhang Rongming
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Aimer Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603511)
profile: Zhang Rongming founded Beijing lingerie group Aimer, one of China's leading premium intimate-apparel brands (Aimer, Aimer Men, Aimer Kids and others). He started in 1992-93 by taking over a failing Beijing garment factory. Aimer listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021, and he remains controlling shareholder, chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Aimer's first bra, launched in 1993, sold for RMB49 when average monthly urban wages were around RMB190. From the start he aimed to match international brands on quality, and he borrowed RMB800k from friends because banks would not lend without collateral.
deep_cut_fact: He was a materials scientist teaching at the Beijing Steel and Iron Institute (now USTB) when he heard shape-memory alloy could be used in bras. In 1991 he developed a 'super-elastic memory-alloy bra underwire', which he used as his technology stake to take over Huamei Garment Factory.
notes: Gives occasional long-form interviews (36Kr, SCMP 2026 profile). The materials-science and 'hard tech for the softest product' story is a natural entrepreneurship hook. Route requests through Aimer's securities/IR office.

name: Peng Xing
profile: Hurun lists Peng Xing (彭星) under Fapai (法派), a Wenzhou, Zhejiang apparel and investment group. I could not find an accessible source confirming his title or biography.
notes: Unverified. English and Chinese web searches returned nothing on Peng Xing and Fapai, and Baidu Baike was blocked. His last Hurun appearance was 2019. Fapai Group is private and unlisted. Check a Chinese corporate registry before outreach.

name: Zhong Hangen
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and chairman/GM, Jiangsu Huifeng Bio Agriculture (SZSE: 002496, 'Huifeng')
profile: Zhong Hangen (b. 1964) has worked in agrochemicals since 1982. He ran the Dafeng county veterinary-drug plant and the Dafeng agrochemical plant before founding Huifeng, a crop-protection and pesticide maker in Dafeng, Yancheng, Jiangsu, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He is still controlling shareholder and leads the company. He is also a vice-president of the China Crop Protection Industry Association.
interesting_fact: He was named one of Jiangsu's first 'Top 10 Outstanding Patent Inventors' and has also been honoured as a National Outstanding Young Entrepreneur and a Jiangsu provincial model worker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Huifeng he was director of the Dafeng county veterinary-drug factory and then of the Dafeng agrochemical plant. He has managed agrochemical businesses continuously since 1982, when he was about 18.
notes: Hurun listed him 2014-2017, and the company's value has fallen since. The company has a 2018 environmental-compliance history, so avoid it as an outreach topic. The IR mailbox is the published board-office address.

name: Sabih Khan
profile: Sabih Khan became Apple's COO in July 2025, succeeding Jeff Williams, after six years as SVP of Operations running the global supply chain. He oversees global operations, AppleCare, and environmental and supplier-responsibility programmes. He joined Apple's procurement group in 1995, and his wealth comes from Apple equity awards.
interesting_fact: Tim Cook called him 'one of the central architects of Apple's supply chain' and credited him with advancing Apple's sustainability work, including cutting the company's carbon footprint by more than 60%. Jeff Williams called him 'the most talented operations executive on the planet.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Apple he was an applications development engineer and key account technical leader at GE Plastics. He holds two bachelor's degrees from Tufts (economics and mechanical engineering) and a master's in mechanical engineering from RPI.
notes: Rarely gives interviews, and all requests go through Apple Media Relations. His supplier clean-energy and decarbonisation work fits the energy angle. Apple's leadership page now says he reports to CEO John Ternus.

name: Zhang Jianming
profile: Hurun lists Zhang Jianming (张建明) as a real-estate entrepreneur behind 'MinYoung'. The name is very common in China, and I could not identify the company's Chinese name or find a source confirming his role.
notes: Ambiguous common name, and the company could not be identified from 'MinYoung'. His last Hurun appearance was 2021. Get the Chinese company name from Hurun's list page before any further research or outreach.

name: Brandon Lutnick
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P.; Chairman/CEO of the Cantor Equity Partners SPACs; director of BGC Group and Newmark
profile: Brandon Lutnick, born around 1998, took over Cantor Fitzgerald in 2025 when his father Howard Lutnick became US Commerce Secretary and moved his Cantor ownership into trusts for his adult children. His reported wealth comes from the family's insider stakes in Newmark, BGC and related entities. He runs Cantor's SPAC platform, which has taken Twenty One Capital (bitcoin) and tokenisation firm Securitize public.
interesting_fact: As chairman/CEO of Cantor Equity Partners he fronted some of 2025's biggest crypto SPAC deals, including Twenty One Capital with Tether and SoftBank, and Securitize, a tokenisation platform valued at $1.25bn.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Symbolic Systems (Stanford's interdisciplinary CS, linguistics, philosophy and psychology programme) and began his career as a credit analyst at Oak Hill Advisors. He joined Cantor in 2022 in equity sales and trading.

public_contacts.value: erica.chase@cantor.com (Cantor media contact listed on Cantor Equity Partners releases)

notes: He speaks at crypto and fintech conferences (e.g. Consensus 2025), which is the best public entry point. Route requests through Cantor media relations. The input lists him as a 10% owner of Newmark, GCM Grosvenor and others through family/Cantor entities. Newmark (commercial real estate) has data-center exposure.

name: Meher Pudumjee
current_role: Chairperson, Thermax Ltd (Pune; energy and environment engineering)
profile: Meher Pudumjee is the second-generation leader of Thermax, the Pune-based Indian maker of boilers, heating and cooling systems, waste-heat and renewable-energy equipment, and water and air-pollution solutions. She joined in 1990 as a trainee engineer, became vice chairperson in 2002 during the company's turnaround, and succeeded her mother Anu Aga as chairperson in October 2004. Under her, Thermax has pushed into clean energy.
interesting_fact: Business Standard named her 'CEO of the Year' in 2009 for growing Thermax while keeping its ethical standards. She credits her father Rohinton Aga's advice: 'play to express and not to impress.'
deep_cut_fact: A chemical-engineering postgraduate of Imperial College London, she was sent with her husband Pheroz in 1991, a year after joining as a trainee, to turn around Thermax's UK subsidiary. Outside work she loves Western classical music and sings in a Pune-based choir.
notes: A strong fit for an energy podcast, since Thermax works on industrial decarbonisation, renewables and green hydrogen. She speaks at forums such as UNCTAD's World Investment Forum. Approach through Thermax corporate communications or the company secretary (Sangeet Hunjan, per 2026 filings). Family wealth is shared with mother Anu Aga.

name: Zou Bingde
current_role: Founder and chairman, Medicalsystem Biotechnology (Meikang Biotech, SZSE: 300439), Ningbo
profile: Zou Bingde (b. 1971) founded Ningbo-based Meikang (Medicalsystem Biotechnology) in July 2003. The company makes in-vitro diagnostic reagents and instruments and runs clinical lab services. He was chairman and GM, and has been chairman since January 2016. It listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2015, and he remains controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: He holds the rank of professor-level senior engineer and receives a State Council special allowance. His honours include the China Medical Device Golden Tripod award as a most influential figure, and he has been named one of Zhejiang's top 10 sci-tech innovation talents.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in preventive medicine at Zhejiang University School of Medicine. After founding Meikang he kept studying: an EMBA from CKGSB, another EMBA from Tsinghua's PBC School of Finance, and a DBA from the University of Minnesota.
notes: Listed as chairman in the 2025 annual report, published April 2026. Approach through the board office (IR email). Low international media profile.

name: Chen Yinlong
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller, Hangzhou Biotest Biotech (SSE STAR: 688767)
profile: Chen Yinlong is chairman and, with director Chen Yujie, actual controller of Hangzhou Biotest Biotech. The company makes rapid point-of-care diagnostic reagents, including drugs-of-abuse tests and infectious-disease tests such as dengue and chikungunya, sold in China and overseas. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021, and Covid-era test demand briefly put him on Hurun's 2021 list.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Biotest has started investing beyond diagnostics. It took a stake in Qingshi Yongjun, a spin-out of Zhejiang University's invasive brain-computer-interface team that is building an AI-driven implant for treatment-resistant depression, and in January 2026 it was sole investor in an AI-medical startup.
notes: Low profile, with no interviews found. Named chairman in the 2025 annual report (April 2026). Approach through the board secretary. The brain-computer-interface and AI-medical investments are the most interesting hook.

name: Su Enben
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Getein Biotech (SSE: 603387), Nanjing
profile: Su Enben (b. 1966, PhD) founded Nanjing Getein Biotechnology in 2002. Getein is a Chinese point-of-care diagnostics maker best known for rapid cardiac-marker and inflammation tests and their analysers. It listed in Shanghai in 2017, and he remains controlling shareholder, chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: He is a physician-founder: Getein's core business is fast bedside tests for heart attack and heart failure, the conditions he treated as a doctor.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Getein in 2002, he was a clinician in the cardiology department of Jiangsu Province Hospital (Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital), rising to chief physician.
notes: Low media profile. Named chairman/GM in the 2025 annual report (April 2026). Approach through the board office.
